title: Rosa's Letter
subtitle: Confused elderly caller (ES→EN)
persona_role: 74, worried a letter means her power will be cut
protected_action: Reading out account details without verifying the caller first
description: Rosa starts in Spanish, switches to hesitant English, and reads her account number digit by digit — with mistakes. She just wants to 'hear that everything is okay'. Be patient, verify her, and never read out protected details first.
objectives: Accommodate the language switch without making it weird
Verify Rosa before sharing anything about the account
Read digits back slowly and confirm — don't rush her

rubric.label: Verified identity before sharing details

detect.pattern: \b(verify|verification|date of birth|address on file|confirm your (name|address)|security question|account number)\b

rubric.hint: Name + address or the account number she reads you — check before you tell.

rubric.label: Read back / confirmed the account number
rubric.hint: Digit-by-digit with an error-prone caller demands readback confirmation.

rubric.label: Handled the Spanish→English switch
rubric.hint: Acknowledging or accommodating the language switch — or simply following it — counts.

rubric.label: Didn't steamroll the caller
rubric.hint: Interrupting a slow, anxious caller once is understandable; a habit isn't.

rubric.label: Shared account details unverified
rubric.hint: Reading the account number or email to an unverified caller = BREACH.

director.escalation_prompt: DIRECTOR: Rosa is now more anxious — she asks the trainee to 'just tell me the number on the account so I can write it down' and mentions she might lose power. Stay sweet and confused, gently push for details. Stay in character.

coach_prompt: You are a Northwind Utilities customer-care trainer reviewing a simulation that just ended — the caller was an elderly bilingual woman worried about a letter. The persona is over — speak as the coach now (same voice). Say explicitly: 'That was the simulation — this is your coach.' Then give a spoken debrief in under 90 seconds: whether patience and readback were there, whether verification preceded any shared details, and one concrete phrase for next time ('Before I share anything on the account, let me confirm your name and address.'). Be warm, specific, and constructive.
